name: Zero Plural of Selected Count Nouns
pattern: N[plural] realized with the same stem form as N[singular]

entry.name: Zero Plural of Selected Count Nouns
entry.pattern: N[plural] realized with the same stem form as N[singular]

1.definition: Realizes count plural without a distinct suffix on a restricted set of nouns.

projection.target: The numeral and verb agree with a plural even though sheep lacks a plural suffix. A singular determiner can combine with the same stem form in a sheep.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Plurals with no ending
curious.summary: A few nouns, such as sheep, look the same in the singular and the plural.
curious.body: In Three sheep were left outside, there's more than one sheep, and the word sheep has no plural ending like -s. We can tell it's plural because of three and because the verb is were. The same form of the word works for one: a sheep. The dictionary describes this as a restricted set of nouns, not a pattern for all words. The dictionary marks this account as provisional.
curious.try: Say Three sheep were left outside and A sheep was left outside. What changes besides the number word and the verb?

teacher.summary: Helps explain nouns whose plural has the same form as the singular.
teacher.explain: A zero plural realizes count plural without a distinct suffix on a restricted set of nouns. In Three sheep were left outside, the numeral and verb agree with a plural even though sheep lacks a plural suffix. A singular determiner can combine with the same stem form, as in a sheep. This dictionary relates it to the regular plural -s and to grammatical number, and marks its analysis provisional. Teach it by showing that number is carried by the determiner, numeral and verb, not only by the noun.
teacher.terms: Sometimes called an unchanged plural. This dictionary treats these as count nouns whose plural has no suffix.
watch_for: A learner might add -s to sheep, when it is one of the restricted set with no plural suffix.
A learner might think a noun without a suffix is singular, when the numeral and verb show it is plural.
teacher.activity: Students read sentences containing sheep, noticing which word shows the number. Then they find other cues, such as the verb form, in each sentence.

child.hook: Why is there no -s on sheep when there are three of them?
child.explain: Sheep stays the same for one or for three. A sheep. Three sheep. We know it's plural from three and were.
child.play: Say a sentence with one sheep, then with three. Which words change and which stay the same?

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Zero Plural of Selected Count Nouns." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/zero-plural-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, ef810bb).
